name: bg-singularity
title: Singularity Background
description: A full-bleed shader that renders something like a black hole: a dark circular void edged with a glowing rim that runs cold blue on one side and warm orange on the other, with wispy gas trailing into black.
use: A space or science-fiction page needs an atmospheric glowing singularity behind its copy.
avoid: It is a full-frame absolute shader whose motion is slow enough that it can read as a still.
a11y: Decorative shader with no reduced-motion check; the white caption only stays readable over the dark centre. (keyboard: n-a, labels: n-a, reduced motion: not handled)
looks: Against pure black sits a large dark disc outlined by a thin luminous ring. The lower-left arc is icy blue and the upper-right arc is warm orange, and faint streaked plumes bleed off the ring toward both corners.
behaves: The ring and its gas drift very slowly, with the plume shape creeping around the rim and the rim fading in and out. There is no input beyond a slow continuous loop.
customise: hue, saturation, brightness, speed, mouseSensitivity, damping and an optional noise setting tune the shader; className adds styles.
weight: heavy: A full-screen fragment shader with a multi-step loop, run every frame.
issues: All six frames differ so little that the moving shader is easy to mistake for a static image.
polishWhy: Intricate rim and gas tendrils with real craft; the motion is too slow to register.
